data.one_liner: Automatically generate Dart models from YAML configuration files.
data.what_it_does: Reads a YAML file defining models, properties, enums, and types, then automatically generates corresponding Dart model classes complete with JSON serialization, equality operators, hash codes, and toString methods.
use_when: You want to maintain model definitions in a centralized YAML format rather than writing Dart classes manually.
You need automated JSON serialization, equals/hashCode, and toString generation for your data models.
avoid_when: You prefer writing your data classes and Freezed/JsonSerializable annotations purely in Dart code.
Your project does not use code generation workflows.
strengths: Supports inline type definitions, generics, enums with properties, and custom converters.
Can look up models from a single config file or an entire directory of YAML files.
weaknesses: Requires managing and writing model definitions in separate YAML files instead of native Dart code.
Breaking changes between major versions (such as v7.0.0) require updates to existing YAML configurations.
data.setup_notes: Add model_generator to your workflow and run via flutter packages run model_generator or specify custom config paths in pubspec.yaml.
